reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: CRM dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep) (E-07), while disputed bills skew toward ACTUAL meter reads (1785) over ESTIMATED reads (1240) (E-01). This pattern indicates the surge is driven by a billing import/validation defect that miscomputes or misissues bills even for accurately-read accounts, not by estimate substitution from missing reads (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE).
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Billing dispute tickets have roughly doubled since August (E-07). The confirmed mechanism: billing-config rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with unit_scaling 'none', compares raw AMI register values against 12-month m3-based consumption history (E-13); firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) report register reads in units of 0.1 m3 rather than m3 (E-12), so BV-17 misreads v4.2 consumption as abnormally high and billing import rejects these timely AMI reads as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, forcing estimate substitution that accounts for 1184 of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (E-11, E-01).
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
